questions.q: How does the summary say you should treat your email inbox?
a: As a processing plant where each message is routed by content
As a destination to check only once a week
As an archive for every message you receive
As a to-do list that stays unread until finished
questions.why: The inbox is an intermediary, not a place where messages should pile up.

questions.q: What should you do with an email task that takes two minutes or less?
a: Do it immediately
Add it to your to-do list
Schedule it for the weekend
Forward it to a colleague
questions.why: The summary says quick tasks should be handled right away, with the rest added to your list.

questions.q: What question should you ask about every piece of media you consume?
a: Is it worth my time, and what will I do with it?
Is it popular with other readers?
Is it free to access?
Is it newly published?
questions.why: The summary says information is only as good as what you use it for.

questions.q: What does the author recommend for a media diet?
a: Keep a handful of regular sources that give you what you need
Follow as many sources as possible to stay informed
Read only books and avoid all video
Rotate sources weekly to avoid blind spots
questions.why: The author cut out news, TV, podcasts and newsletters after finding they added no value.

questions.q: What does frontloading mean in your communication?
a: Putting the most important information first, with enough context
Sending fewer messages and shorter replies
Answering every message within minutes
Using bullet points instead of paragraphs
questions.why: Frontloading means getting to the point, backing it up, and ending.
